overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. A single-member (subquorum) attendance at a 2018 workshop was not a meeting, and the conflict-of-interest claims fall outside the OML and were referred to the State Ethics Commission.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board deliberated outside a posted meeting by taking part in a 2018 workshop with the Town Administrator and other public bodies' chairs on a transfer station.
allegations.key_passage: As such, because only one member of the Board, a subquorum, attended and participated in the workshop, the Board did not hold a “meeting” for the purposes of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged an informal workshop of public officials (chairs of several bodies) was itself a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Further, we note that an informal gathering of public officials - here, the chairs of various public bodies - does not constitute a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint seemed to allege the Zoning Board of Appeals and Planning Board also violated the OML by attending the workshop, but was filed only with the Board.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any allegations that the Zoning Board of Appeals or Planning Board violated the Open Meeting Law because we find that the complaint was not properly filed with either of those public bodies.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a Board member had a conflict of interest because he also sat on the ZBA and took part in a December 16, 2019 joint discussion of the transfer station.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review these allegations and refer the complainant to the State Ethics Commission, which enforces the Commonwealth’s Conflict of Interest Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board 'instructed and lectured' other bodies and gave unsubstantiated facts about the transfer station, creating a conflict of interest.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government’s statutory authority concerns compliance only with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
